subject: Pilot Mutual Action Plan & Acceptance Gates — EverCare
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@evercare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot kickoff recap and proposed MOP (next steps)

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier — appreciated you and Samir walking us through the evaluation priorities. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed Mutual Action Plan (attached) and the acceptance gates so we have a single source of truth for the pilot. High-level recap:

- Primary objective: Measure generation latency and cost-per-1K tokens on EverCare anonymized routing queries and confirm model parity on the 3 critical prompts you showed (~70-90 tokens).
- Success criteria (proposal): 95th percentile latency <= 450ms over representative load; average token cost reduction vs current baseline >= 20%; no functional regressions on the 3 canonical prompts (pass/fail test set).
- Timeline: 3-week pilot window (Dec 8–Dec 29) with a short smoke test next week and a full ingest on Dec 13.
- Ownership: Redwood – Jonas (sales/technical lead), Marissa (customer success for onboarding/ops). EverCare – Elaine (product), Samir (platform/security).

Attached: mop_evercare_v1.pdf (MOP draft), redwood-sla-summary.pdf (SLA and fallback options). Also added a checklist for firewall/network (network-firewall-checklist.xlsx) for your infra team.

Concrete asks for EverCare before the smoke test:
1) Confirm the three canonical prompts and provide the masked test set (S3 link or Drive) by EOD Monday Dec 7.
2) Give us a list of IPs and egress rules to validate the firewall checklist by Tuesday (Dec 9).
3) Confirm whether telemetry with masked IDs is acceptable or if you need payload-level redaction handled by our side.

I put a Drive link in the doc for collaborative edits. If this looks good, we’ll lock the MOP Tuesday and schedule the smoke test for Dec 10 (30–45 minute window).

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@evercare.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@evercare.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap and proposed MOP (next steps)

Jonas — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

- Prompts/test set: We can deliver a masked test set (500 items) by Monday EOD. We will mark the three canonical prompts in the README.
- Firewall/IPs: Our infra lead is OOO Mon-Tue, but I can share a temporary whitelist for the smoke window. Full firewall changes will be scheduled for Dec 9 as you suggested.
- Telemetry: We prefer telemetry with only hashed identifiers. If Redwood can accept hashed IDs instead of payload-level redaction, that would keep things simpler.

Two additional asks:
1) Can you confirm expected peak concurrent requests for the smoke test? (We need to size the network path).
2) What rollback options do we have if we observe higher error rates during the ingest window?

Samir — looping you for network confirmation (you can reply with the whitelist IPs).

Thanks,
Elaine

--
Elaine Chen
Head of Product, EverCare Health
elaine.chen@evercare.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@evercare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@evercare.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap and proposed MOP (next steps)

Elaine — perfect, thanks. A few quick answers and updates: 

- Peak concurrent for smoke test: plan for 60 concurrent connections (burst up to 120 for 30s) — that’s a lightweight smoke to exercise batching and KV warm-up. We’ll provide exact source IPs (Redwood smoke cluster) before the window.
- Rollback plan: default is immediate traffic cut and auto-fallback to the baseline model endpoint you currently use (we’ll coordinate a DNS/traffic switchback). Engineer on-call will watch metrics with an automated rollback trigger at 3% error-rate increase or 2x latency on the 95th percentile. Details in the MOP doc.

I updated the MOP in Drive and attached an exported PDF (mop_evercare_v1.pdf) for your legal procurement. Also dropped short items for Marissa and Priyom — Marissa, can you confirm onboarding calendar and who will run the ingest? Priyom, any infra caveats on our side for the production-like ingest?

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@evercare.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@evercare.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2026 14:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot Mutual Action Plan & Acceptance Gates — EverCare

Hi all — looping in operational details and owners from Redwood’s side. Quick notes: 

- Onboarding/calendar: I’m available to lead the ingest on Dec 13 at 10am PT. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short runbook and the ingest checklist.
- Ingest owner: Redwood will run the ingest (Marissa) with EverCare monitoring on their side (Samir). Please confirm a Slack channel or PagerDuty pairing for the window.
- Network checklist: Priyom — please confirm the egress IPs and whether TLS inspection could rewrite headers (we need to know for telemetry hashing).

Next steps before the ingest:
1) EverCare to share masked test set + confirmation of canonical prompts (deadline: Mon Dec 8 EOD).
2) Samir to provide temporary whitelist for smoke test and schedule full firewall change by Dec 9.
3) Legal/Procurement: Elaine, the attached SLA summary and MOP export should be enough for preliminary procurement review; if your team needs a contract redline we can loop legal.

Marissa
